world.description: a pencil logistics and supply network

world.label: Pencil Supply Network
world.summary: A recurring network moves materials through pencil makers and shops to customers.

actions.description: Gather logs for the timber supply.
Process graphite ore into pencil graphite.
Assemble pencils from boards and graphite.
Carry a counted quantity of one kind of goods from one business to another.
Sell pencils from the shop to a customer.

mechanics.rationale: The forest crew gathers logs into its represented inventory.
limits: Only the forest crew's logs inventory changes; gathering does not directly move logs to another business.
tests: A positive quantity adds that many logs for the forest crew.
Zero or negative quantity is refused.
A different worker role cannot gather timber.

mechanics.rationale: The sawmill consumes logs and produces the same quantity of boards.
limits: The represented inventory does not specify processing yield or waste, so boards produced equal logs consumed.
tests: With enough logs, the requested logs are consumed and boards added.
Insufficient logs and nonpositive quantities are refused.
A workshop with another role cannot saw boards.
semantic_bindings: quantity counts logs sawn and boards produced

mechanics.rationale: The graphite miners gather ore into their represented inventory.
limits: Only the miners' graphite ore inventory changes.
tests: A positive quantity adds that much ore.
Zero or negative quantity is refused.
A worker with another role cannot gather ore.

mechanics.rationale: The graphite works consumes ore and produces the same quantity of pencil graphite.

checks.label: the graphite works has enough ore

limits: The represented inventory does not specify processing yield or waste, so graphite produced equals ore consumed.
tests: With enough ore, ore is consumed and graphite added in equal quantities.
Insufficient ore and nonpositive quantities are refused.
A workshop with another role cannot process graphite.
semantic_bindings: quantity counts ore processed and graphite produced

mechanics.rationale: The pencil factory assembles pencils from an equal quantity of boards and graphite.
limits: One board and one unit of graphite are consumed per pencil because no alternative recipe or yield is represented.
tests: With enough of both inputs, the factory consumes each input and adds the requested pencils.
Insufficient inputs and nonpositive quantities are refused.
A worker with another role cannot assemble pencils.
semantic_bindings: quantity counts pencils made and units of boards and graphite consumed

mechanics.rationale: The carrier transfers a counted quantity of boards between the named businesses, subtracting from the source and adding to the destination.

checks.label: the carrier moves goods between businesses

limits: This mechanic supports boards only; other goods are refused because a single static path cannot safely select among inventory fields.
The named source and destination must each have inventory; this mechanic does not verify business categories.
tests: A positive boards transfer subtracts from the source and adds the same quantity to a different destination.
Insufficient source stock, identical endpoints, nonpositive quantities, and goods other than boards are refused.

mechanics.rationale: The pencil shop transfers pencils to a customer and reduces that customer's waiting orders by the sold quantity.

checks.label: the shop stocks and sells pencils
the customer is waiting for enough pencils

limits: Sale is limited to a customer with represented waiting orders and available shop stock; no payment state is represented.
tests: A sale within shop stock and customer demand transfers pencils and reduces waiting orders equally.
Insufficient stock or demand and nonpositive quantities are refused.
A worker with another role cannot sell pencils.
semantic_bindings: quantity counts pencils sold and customer waiting orders served

processes.rationale: The represented forest source renews logs over time so timber gathering can continue.
The represented mine renews graphite ore over time so ore gathering can continue.
Customers continue to want pencils, replenishing their represented waiting demand after sales.

readout.title: How coordination slowed (the four mechanisms of the Waltzman paper)
readout.summary: Forest Crew repeatedly gathered timber and Graphite Miners repeatedly gathered ore, while the world replenished both resources. Customer demand at the bookshop and school increased each round; no coordination or decision process is recorded.
